entries.note: Cao 2016 (PMID 27099175) abstract quote verbatim. Neuronal excitability/heat firing has no measured human counterpart in NCT01769274 (PI-NRS only); untested/not_measured holds.

Registry arm text verbatim (results posted 2019-11-19). Untested is right for the iPSC track, but iPSC was not the system dose relied on: PBPK/IC50 model (Jones 2016) stated a target and matched SAD PK; see missing.
Cox 2006 (PMID 17167479) quote verbatim in abstract. Opening untested fine; genetics track arguably opens 2004 (IEM gain-of-function, Yang 2004), proxy acceptable.

Goldberg 2012 (PMID 22035805, epub 2011-10-28) quote verbatim; abstract itself frames CIP/IEM opposite-phenotype model. NCT01090622 primary is pain intensity difference, consistent. Topical NCT01486446 and PF-05089771 registry means also favour drug; no contra.

Cao 2016 quote verbatim. Lines derived from trial subjects, trial completed 2013-07, published with results: retrodiction/retro correct. Registry primary 2.08 vs 2.73, 1.95 vs 2.04, untested statistically, direction matches.

entries.note: DOI resolves to Jones 2016 Clin Pharmacokinet (PMID 26895021); quote verbatim in abstract. Opening untested at 2010 (microdose NCT01165736 start, before SAD) is an allowed proxy; class-level, in_silico, tier 1 correct.

entries.rule: Dose: target reached = same; healthy-volunteer PK counts
entries.note: Quote verbatim in abstract; PBPK stated 1 g for ~12x IC50 Cmax before the SAD study (2010-12), so prospective, not retro. SAD PK 'compared well' = target reached; comparison_stated true, 2016 correct. Fold error unknown (abstract only).

missing: Dose track: PBPK model from a healthy-volunteer microdose study (Jones et al. 2016, Clin Pharmacokinet, doi:10.1007/s40262-015-0365-0, PMID 26895021; model_kind in_silico, product_in_model true). Stated: 'PBPK model for PF-05089771 predicted a 1 g oral dose would be required to achieve exposures of approximately 12x Nav1.7 IC50 at Cmax'; 'In a subsequent single ascending oral dose clinical study, the predictions for PF-05089771 compared well with observed data.' Healthy-volunteer PK counts: dose same, comparison_stated true, 2016. This model, not iPSC neurons, set the IEM dose (1600 mg). Whether Cao 2016 reports IEM-patient exposure vs the IC50 multiple was not checked (paywalled).

Possible dose/engagement context: Siebenga et al. 2020 (Clin Transl Sci, PMC7070789) healthy-volunteer evoked-pain battery found no PF-05089771 analgesia. It is a human readout, not a model compared with patients, so likely no new track; listed for the drafter to rule out.
rule_questions: Patient-level genotype-to-drug-response predictions in IEM (structural modelling plus iPSC/DRG functional profiling predicting carbamazepine response of Nav1.7-V400M/S241T; Yang 2012 Nat Commun, Geha 2016 JAMA Neurol) use a non-selective drug outside the member list. Under the class rule they do not score, but the brief does not say whether a patient-level model validated only on a non-member drug should be listed as an untested track for the class.

Funapide (XEN402) is described in some sources as a broader Nav blocker (Nav1.7 plus other subtypes). The tile lists it as a member; checker accepted the given class table without re-deciding selectivity.
